Baby Beet Bisque

Served at: Feast of the Holy Innocents (Childermas Banquet)

Serves 4-6Prep 25 minCook 50 min

This vibrant Baby Beet Bisque offers a comforting and visually striking dish for the Childermas Banquet, also known as the Feast of the Holy Innocents. Its deep crimson hue and velvety texture provide warmth and a gentle elegance, serving as a thoughtful remembrance on a day dedicated to reflection and solemn commemoration. The use of 'baby' beets subtly echoes the theme of the holiday, offering a dish that is both nourishing and symbolically resonant.

Ingredients

  • 1.5 pounds (680 g) baby beets, trimmed, scrubbed, and greens removed (reserve some small greens for garnish if desired)
  • 2 tablespoons (30 ml) olive oil, divided
  • 1 medium yellow onion, chopped
  • 2 cloves garlic, minced
  • 4 cups (960 ml) vegetable broth or chicken broth
  • 1/2 cup (120 ml) heavy cream (or full-fat coconut milk for dairy-free)
  • 1 tablespoon (15 ml) fresh lemon juice
  • Salt and freshly ground black pepper to taste
  • Optional garnish: fresh dill, a dollop of sour cream or crème fraîche, or finely chopped reserved beet greens

Method

  1. Preheat oven to 400°F (200°C). Toss the trimmed baby beets with 1 tablespoon (15 ml) olive oil, salt, and pepper on a baking sheet.
  2. Roast beets for 30-40 minutes, or until tender when pierced with a fork. Let cool slightly, then peel the skins (they should slip off easily). Roughly chop the roasted beets.
  3. In a large pot or Dutch oven, heat the remaining 1 tablespoon (15 ml) olive oil over medium heat. Add the chopped onion and cook until softened, about 5-7 minutes.
  4. Add the minced garlic and cook for another minute until fragrant.
  5. Stir in the chopped roasted beets and vegetable broth. Bring to a simmer, then reduce heat and cook for 10-15 minutes to allow flavors to meld.
  6. Carefully transfer the soup to a blender (or use an immersion blender) and blend until completely smooth.
  7. Return the blended soup to the pot. Stir in the heavy cream and lemon juice. Heat gently until warmed through, but do not boil.
  8. Season with additional salt and pepper to taste.
  9. Ladle the bisque into bowls and garnish as desired with fresh dill, a dollop of sour cream, or finely chopped reserved beet greens.

Tips

  • For an even smoother bisque, pass the blended soup through a fine-mesh sieve after blending.
  • Add a pinch of ground ginger or a tiny amount of grated fresh ginger to the soup for a subtle warming spice note.
  • To make this recipe vegan, ensure your broth is vegetable-based and use full-fat coconut milk instead of heavy cream.
